But likely they just want current time difference. We can compute based on standard offsets: Los Angeles (Pacific Time) UTC-8 normally, but with DST it's UTC-7. Then find first Sunday of November 2026: November has 30 days. Day-of-week for Nov 1: Need to compute offset from Jan 1. Days from Jan 1 to Nov 1: Jan(31)+Feb(28)+Mar(31)+Apr(30)+May(31)+Jun(30)+Jul(31)+Aug(31)+Sep(30)+Oct(31)=?? Sum: 31+28=59, +31=90, +30=120, +31=151, +30=181, +31=212, +31=243, +30=273, +31=304. So Nov 1 is day 305 of year. Jan 1 is day 1. Difference 304 days. 304 mod 7 = 304 - 7*43=304-301=3. So shift by 3 days forward. Jan 1 Thursday +3 days = Sunday. So Nov 1 2026 is Sunday. Therefore first Sunday is Nov 1. DST ends at 2am local time on Nov 1. So as of Nov 4, 2026, both are on standard time: LA PST (UTC-8), Berlin CET (UTC+1). So time difference is 9 hours ahead: Berlin is 9 hours ahead of LA.
